item.title: Surprisingly Complex Waves Reveal the Brain's Inner Workings
item.description:
📝 Home Surprisingly Complex Waves Reveal the Brain’s Inner Workings Comment Save Article Read Later Share Facebook Copied. In a study published in April 2026 in Nature Communications, neuroscientists measured traveling waves of neural activity and observed a menagerie: source waves that appear to emanate from one location, sink waves that converge on a spot, and vortexlike spiral waves. Joshua Jacobs and Anup Das were part of a team that observed complex patterns of brain waves using intracranial electrodes.
🔗 Read more: https://www.quantamagazine.org/surprisingly-complex-waves-reveal-the-brains-inner-workings-20260930/

item.title: Functional Ultrasound Imaging (fUSI) from scratch
item.description:
📝 Functional ultrasound imaging from scratchA new modality is coming to brain imagingPatrick MineaultSep 30, 202672ShareFunctional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) is a brain imaging modality that is just starting to be demonstrated in human studies. Functional ultrasound instead captures movies of brain tissue very rapidly, tracking subtle changes caused by the blood flow that follows neural activity. How fUSI works at a high levelFunctional ultrasound imaging, like conventional ultrasound imaging, uses transducers—which act as both transmitters and receivers—to communicate ultrasound through tissue.

item.title: Before pixels: Modular industrial dashboards
item.description:
📝 This was a very cool physical display for air traffic control, at the The Deutsches Museum in Münich: At Fernmeldemuseum Stuttgart, these were used to monitor subway trains, or light rail. I do imagine these panels must have been interactive with all the buttons. A railway museum in Nuremberg used what looks like the exact same system, and I spotted a few modules with their plates removed: And, here’s a similar panel shown in a tram museum in Stuttgart, filled with an incredible typographical tension between DIN and the German equivalent of Dymo: Warsaw’s train museum had a slightly different system, but similar in look and feel: This big industrial switch toggled between day and night.
🔗 Read more: https://unsung.aresluna.org/before-pixels-modular-industrial-dashboards/

item.title: Hacking SimCity 2000 saved games
item.description:
